title: PoseBridge: Bridging the Skeletonization Gap for Zero-Shot Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
claim: Prior methods align text with skeletons after information is already lost; ours routes upstream pose-side cues into alignment to disambiguate similar actions.
layout: Left input column plus two stacked pipeline panels (A prior, B ours), left-to-right
description: The left column shows RGB frame sequences. A blue 'Target sample' (put on a hat/cap) sits above a pink 'Confusing samples' group (headphones, glasses). Two stacked panels sit to the right. Panel A, in gray, is the conventional pipeline: pose estimator, predicted skeleton, skeleton encoder, and a text encoder fed by action-class text. Both encoders feed a semantic space, shown as an ellipse. A red X and trash can mark the lost action semantics (hat, headphone and glasses icons). The result is a muddled bar chart with a confused face. Panel B, in warm orange, is PoseBridge. It has the same pipeline plus an orange branch that extracts pose-anchored semantics. These pass through a Semantic Bridge and Prototype Adaptation into the encoders. The result is a clear bar chart with a smiley face. A legend identifies the target and confusing text prototypes.
caption: Motivation of PoseBridge. (A) Conventional S2A aligns text with joint-coordinate skeletons after skeletonization, where object, interaction, and pose-relative cues are not explicit. (B) PoseBridge routes HPE-side cues to the alignment space, disambiguating object-sensitive actions with similar skeleton trajectories.
abstract: Zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition (ZSSAR) is typically treated as a skeleton-text alignment problem: encode joint-coordinate sequences, align them with language, and classify unseen actions. We argue that this alignment is often too late. Skeletons are not complete action observations, but compressed outputs of human pose estimation (HPE); by the time alignment begins, human-object interactions and pose-relative visual cues may no longer be explicit. We call this upstream semantic loss. To address it, we propose PoseBridge, an HPE-aware ZSSAR framework that bridges intermediate HPE representations to skeleton-text alignment. Rather than adding an RGB action branch or object detector, PoseBridge extracts pose-anchored semantic cues from the same HPE process that produces skeletons, then transfers them through skeleton-conditioned bridging and semantic prototype adaptation. Across NTU-RGB+D 60/120, PKU-MMD, and Kinetics-200/400, PoseBridge improves ZSSAR performance under the evaluated protocols. On the Kinetics-200/400 PURLS benchmark, which contains in-the-wild videos with diverse scenes and action contexts, PoseBridge achieves substantial gains over prior ZSSAR methods, outperforming the strongest compared baseline by 13.3-17.4 points across all eight splits. Code is available at https://github.com/hyeon0819/PoseBridge.
